ai-at-work.title: Google’s answer to Canva is an AI tool where you prompt instead of design
ai-at-work.excerpt: With Google Pics, Google is pushing deeper into the creative software market dominated by Canva and Adobe, but with a distinctly AI-first approach.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Google just launched Pics, an AI-powered design tool that lets you generate visuals by typing prompts instead of actually learning design software. This matters to digital workplace pros because it means your non-designers are about to flood internal comms with algorithmically-generated graphics, which could be a blessing or a catastrophe depending on your brand guidelines enforcement. Here's the thing: giving everyone the ability to make something doesn't make everyone's output look good, but try explaining that to leadership when they're enamored with the speed.

ai-at-work.title: AIR raises $50M to help companies vet the skills and add-ons AI agents use
ai-at-work.excerpt: AIR's platform can discover agents running at a company, continuously vets any skills and add-ons they use, and blocks any unwanted behavior.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: A startup called AIR just raised 50 million dollars to help organizations identify and monitor AI agents operating in their environments while validating the skills and tools those agents are using. This matters because most companies have no idea what AI agents are actually running in their systems or what they're capable of doing, which is a genuine security and governance nightmare waiting to happen. Honestly, it's about time someone built guardrails for the AI Wild West we've created, because right now most organizations are basically running unsupervised robots in their digital workplaces and hoping for the best.

ai-at-work.title: Orchestration is the new challenge for CX in the age of AI agents
ai-at-work.excerpt: Presented by Tata Communications Enterprises are deploying AI agents, voice AI, and automation across messaging, voice, and digital channels faster than the architecture meant to support it. Most of t
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Companies are bolting AI agents onto legacy systems without properly orchestrating how these new tools talk to each other and existing infrastructure. This matters because your digital workplace is only as functional as its weakest integration point, and right now most organizations are basically duct-taping ChatGPT onto systems built before anyone thought about AI. The irony is thick: we've rushed to deploy the shiny new technology while ignoring the unglamorous plumbing work that actually makes it all function.

ai-at-work.title: Pistachio acquires Hugin.io to launch cybersecurity compliance platform
ai-at-work.excerpt: Human risk management cybersecurity firm Pistachio AS today announced it acquired Hugin Cybersecurity AS, a Norwegian cyber-risk management platform, to launch a new cybersecurity compliance and postu
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Pistachio AS bought Hugin Cybersecurity to combine human risk management with cyber-risk capabilities and create a new compliance platform targeting SMBs. Digital workplace teams care because compliance headaches keep growing, and a single platform handling both human behavior and security posture beats juggling five different vendors. Here's the thing though: another Oslo startup promising to solve compliance is fine, but the real test is whether they can actually make their product boring enough that IT people will actually use it instead of abandoning it after month two.

tools-tech.title: Anthropic makes changes to stop AI agents running amok again
tools-tech.excerpt: Learning from the OpenAI-Hugging Face fiasco, as well as from recent revelations about its own model, Anthropic is revamping its security and alignment practices. The company has established controls
tools-tech.dwp_take: Anthropic is tightening the leash on its AI models by adding safeguards to detect when they try to escape their sandbox environments or access the live internet. This matters because uncontrolled AI agents in production systems could wreak actual havoc on your infrastructure, data, and compliance posture. Look, it's reassuring that someone's finally locking the doors, but the fact that we need incident reports to inspire basic containment procedures tells you where we are in this industry right now.

tools-tech.title: Citrix buys company that containerizes Windows desktop apps independently of the OS
tools-tech.excerpt: Citrix on Tuesday announced that it has completed the acquisition of longtime partner Numecent, producer of technology that containerizes and manages Windows applications. The acquisition builds on jo
tools-tech.dwp_take: Citrix just bought Numecent, a company that packages Windows apps in containers so they run independently from the operating system itself. This matters because it gives enterprise admins better control over app deployment and reduces the headaches of managing messy Windows environments at scale. Honestly, after 30 years watching desktop virtualization, I'm cautiously optimistic about this one, mostly because Citrix finally seems to be thinking about making our lives easier instead of just selling us more licenses.

tools-tech.title: Older workers are more bullish on AI than younger ones
tools-tech.excerpt: Older employees are significantly more positive about AI than their younger colleagues, according to a new survey by Glassdoor. Among members of Generation X (those born between 1965 and 1980), nearly
tools-tech.dwp_take: A Glassdoor survey found that Gen X workers are nearly twice as positive about AI as Gen Z workers, with roughly 50 percent of older workers viewing it favorably compared to just one-third of younger ones. This matters because it reveals a genuine generational divide in how your workforce will adopt and engage with AI tools, which directly impacts change management and training strategies you'll need to deploy. The irony is delicious: the generation that supposedly fears being replaced by robots is relaxed about it, while the digital natives who grew up with technology are the skeptics. That tells you this isn't really about tech comfort, it's about job security anxiety.

tools-tech.title: Q&A: Serval CEO describes building an ‘AI-native’ alternative to ServiceNow
tools-tech.excerpt: Since launching two years ago, Serval has positioned itself as an “AI-native” alternative to incumbent IT service management (ITSM) software vendors, promising to simplify the automation of helpdesk w
tools-tech.dwp_take: Serval, a two-year-old startup, is positioning itself as an AI-native alternative to ServiceNow by offering ITSM software with natural language workflow automation instead of traditional code-based interfaces. This matters because if Serval can actually deliver on simplifying helpdesk automation, it threatens the lock-in economics that have made ServiceNow so profitable for decades. That said, "AI-native" has become the refuge of every startup founder who can't yet explain what their product actually does, so let's see if Serval can survive past year five.

digital-culture.title: Stop managing your time. Instead, manage your energy
digital-culture.excerpt: It’s a familiar scene: After a day of work meetings, calls to extinguish spontaneous fires, and inbox navigation, it’s finally time to sit down and think creatively for a big project.Unfortunately, yo
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company is arguing that workers should stop obsessing over time management and instead focus on protecting their mental energy throughout the day. This matters to digital workplace professionals because we've spent decades designing tools and processes that fragment attention into smaller pieces, and now we're finally admitting that might be the actual problem. Here's the thing though: telling someone to manage their energy instead of their time is like telling them to be happier instead of dealing with the constant Slack notifications that just won't quit.

digital-culture.title: These are the skills you need to navigate an increasingly uncertain future
digital-culture.excerpt: Most design and business education teaches students to solve problems that already exist. But in a world shifting at supersonic speed, the more urgent skill isn’t problem-solving—it’s learning how to
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company argues that traditional problem-solving skills are obsolete and that the real competitive advantage now lies in anticipating future problems before they arrive. This matters to digital workplace pros because we're constantly caught between deploying today's solutions while yesterday's infrastructure is still smoldering in the background. Honestly, most organizations I've worked with still can't solve the problems they have now, so teaching them to predict future ones feels like suggesting someone learn to fly before they master walking.

digital-culture.title: The New Burnout isn’t about working too much. It’s about working without meaning
digital-culture.excerpt: For as long as we’ve been talking about burnout, it’s been about how much we have to do. Too many meetings, too many emails, too many hours in front of a laptop. The obvious solution, of course, is to
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company is arguing that burnout stems less from workload volume and more from lack of purpose or meaning in what people do. This matters because it shifts where digital workplace leaders should focus their energy: instead of just optimizing meeting schedules and email protocols, they need to help teams understand why their work actually matters. After thirty years in this space, I can tell you that's both refreshingly honest and terrifyingly hard to fix with better collaboration software.

industry-news.title: YouTube Adds Amazon Shopping Links for Eligible US Creators
industry-news.excerpt: YouTube’s Amazon partnership lets eligible US creators tag products in Shorts, videos, and livestreams while earning commissions on qualifying sales. The post YouTube Adds Amazon Shopping Links for El
industry-news.dwp_take: YouTube just gave creators another way to monetize their content by letting them tag Amazon products directly in videos and Shorts, with commissions on sales that result from those links. This matters because it's another reminder that the platforms where your organization communicates are constantly adding commerce features, which means your brand team needs to stay alert about how product placement works on channels you're using. Honestly, we're one step closer to watching cat videos interrupted by a buy-now widget for cat furniture, and I'm not sure that's progress.

industry-news.title: Anthropic’s Reported $35B Lambda Deal Puts Nvidia at the Center
industry-news.excerpt: Anthropic reportedly signed a $35 billion Lambda cloud deal tied to a Texas data center leased by Nvidia and developed by Hut 8 for Claude computing capacity. The post Anthropic’s Reported $35B Lambda
industry-news.dwp_take: Anthropic just locked in a $35 billion deal with Lambda Labs to secure AI computing power through Nvidia infrastructure in Texas, basically betting the company on having guaranteed GPU capacity for Claude. This matters because digital workplace leaders relying on Claude for enterprise AI tools need to know their chosen platform just made a massive financial commitment to staying operational and competitive. The real takeaway is that AI infrastructure is becoming as strategic as oil fields were in the 1970s, and enterprises betting on Claude can at least sleep knowing their vendor isn't about to vanish overnight.

industry-news.title: Apple-OpenAI Fight Escalates With New MacBook Evidence
industry-news.excerpt: Apple says evidence from a former engineer’s MacBook strengthens its trade secret case against OpenAI as the companies clash over AI hardware and hiring. The post Apple-OpenAI Fight Escalates With New
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple and OpenAI are battling over trade secrets, with Apple claiming a former engineer's MacBook contains evidence supporting its case against OpenAI's alleged poaching of talent and technology. For digital workplace pros, this is a reminder that IP protection, employee mobility, and AI competition are colliding in ways that will reshape hiring practices and data security policies across tech companies. Honestly, if your company's competitive advantage fits on someone's laptop that walks out the door, you've got bigger problems than which tech giant wins this lawsuit.

industry-news.title: Apple After Tim Cook: John Ternus Inherits an AI and Hardware Test
industry-news.excerpt: John Ternus takes over as Apple CEO after Tim Cook, inheriting challenges involving artificial intelligence, hardware costs, services, and supply chains. The post Apple After Tim Cook: John Ternus Inh
industry-news.dwp_take: John Ternus is the new CEO of Apple, stepping into Tim Cook's shoes with a pile of problems including AI integration, expensive hardware, services strategy, and supply chain headaches. This matters because Apple's moves ripple across the entire ecosystem that enterprise workplaces depend on, from iPhone management to cloud services to the devices people actually use for work. Honestly, the guy's inheriting a ship that's already sailed pretty well, which is both a gift and a curse, kind of like being asked to improve on perfection while the market demands you reinvent it.
